absent: Locking discipline for interrupt descriptor tables and tick counter updates and message descriptor lists.
Semantics and side effects of architecture specific interrupt disable and enable and save and restore and halt primitives.
Numeric values of tick frequency and tick rate and user tick frequency and nanoseconds per tick.
Storage and update path for the global tick counter and runtime conversion helpers and clock tick conversion.
Time type width and maximum time value and generic division routine and calendar conversion details.
Complete parameter list and contract for the message writer callback beyond the descriptor argument.
Implementations behind descriptor insertion and removal and lookup and next active search and firmware translation.

findings.text: Each examined header establishes a unique inclusion guard that marks the header as seen and prevents repeated processing within one translation unit.
Both critical timing markers in this configuration are inert statement safe operations with no state change and no ordering effect.

Raw local interrupt controls forward to architecture specific counterparts for disabling and enabling and saving and restoring and flag reading and disabled testing and halting. Forms that carry a flag word require an unsigned long object. Restore performs bogus state validation before forwarding.
Bogus restore detection has two build variants with one fully inert and the other warning when a restore is requested while the architecture reports interrupts currently enabled.

Halt support has a tracing variant that marks hard interrupts enabled before halting and a direct variant that only halts. Flag reading is aliased to the raw reader. Disabled state query is either derived from a freshly saved flag word or read directly from the architecture. Saved flag testing is aliased to the raw tester.
Trace state records a total event count plus for hard enable and hard disable and soft enable and soft disable both the address where the transition occurred and the associated event identifier.
An interrupt flow handler is a callback that receives the descriptor for the interrupt being processed and returns no value.

Descriptor iteration snapshots the total count once then walks every index forward mapping each number to a descriptor and skipping absent entries. Reverse iteration starts at the highest index and moves downward. Active iteration follows a next active accessor from zero. Numeric iteration walks the raw index range without descriptor lookup.

Handler results use zero for none and one for handled and two for wake thread. A helper maps any nonzero input to handled and zero to none. A typedef aliases the enumeration as the handler return type.
The tick shift constant takes integer values four through thirteen across ten mutually exclusive configurations increasing by one per configuration.

Scaled division combines a shifted quotient with a rounded shifted remainder. The hardware divider and the tick length in microseconds and the user tick length in microseconds are each computed with half denominator rounding from tick rate and kernel or user tick frequency.
Current tick counter accessor widens the global tick value to sixty four bits and returns it.

Thirty two bit time comparisons tolerate counter wrap by interpreting the difference as signed. After and before are inverses and equality forms include equality and closed range requires both inclusive bounds and half open range excludes the upper bound.
Sixty four bit comparisons apply the same wrap tolerant signed difference logic using sixty four bit operands with inverse before forms and an inclusive range helper.

Jiffies relative helpers compare a supplied stamp against the live tick counter using the wrap tolerant predicates with thirty two bit forms reading the counter directly and sixty four bit forms reading through the sixty four bit accessor covering strict and inclusive before and after.
Initial tick value corresponds to negative three hundred seconds worth of ticks. Maximum usable offset is half the signed long maximum minus one. Printable timestamp buffer size is thirty.

Second scale shift is thirty one or thirty two minus the tick shift depending on configuration. Nanosecond shift adds twenty nine. Second and nanosecond conversion factors scale by those shifts with round up division by tick length. Maximum whole seconds representable in ticks has two configuration specific derivations from maximum offset and tick length and scale.

Conversion from ticks to milliseconds and microseconds and nanoseconds scales linearly by the per tick unit count. Microsecond conversion rejects at build time configurations where tick frequency exceeds one million per second. Nanosecond conversion builds on the microsecond result.

Reverse conversions round up to whole ticks and cap excessive inputs at maximum offset. Variants cover evenly divisible frequencies and high frequency multiplication and generic fixed point scaling. Millisecond conversion saturates negative compile time constants and dispatches compile time versus runtime inputs to different implementations. Second conversion multiplies by tick frequency. Microsecond conversion mirrors the millisecond structure with its own overflow cap.
Delta helpers replace negative tick deltas with zero before converting to clock ticks or milliseconds so past deadlines report zero rather than a large wrapped value.

Construction from seconds and nanoseconds saturates to the maximum representable time when seconds reach the implementation limit otherwise combining seconds scaled to nanoseconds with the nanosecond remainder. Calendar structure conversion delegates to this constructor.
Time addition is plain integer addition of the two operands. Unsafe addition uses unsigned sixty four bit arithmetic. Nanosecond subtraction subtracts a plain integer offset.
Comparison returns negative or zero or positive for less or equal or greater. After and before predicates test the sign of that result.

Division of a time value rejects negative divisors by trapping or warning depending on configuration. One configuration accelerates compile time constant divisors that fit in thirty two bits by dividing the magnitude and restoring sign otherwise delegating to a generic routine. The other performs direct division after the negative divisor check.

Conversion to microseconds and milliseconds divides by the corresponding nanosecond count. Delta helpers subtract two times then convert. Addition and subtraction of microsecond and millisecond offsets scale the offset to nanoseconds before applying it.

Conditional conversion to calendar form writes the output and reports success only for nonzero inputs leaving the output untouched for zero. Microsecond and millisecond constructors scale their input by the matching nanoseconds per unit factor.

Message address low and address high and data are each exposed both as a plain thirty two bit word and as an architecture specific packed wrapper holding one thirty two bit field allowing the same storage to be viewed either way.
Isolated message detection always reports false. Cached message retrieval and sysfs population and sysfs teardown are inert operations that do nothing and report success where a status is returned.

Device message descriptor overlays mask and control words and packs capability flags and sharing attributes with a default interrupt number and overlays a mask position byte with a mask register base pointer.

Domain cookie overlays an integer value and a generic pointer and an input output pointer. Descriptor index limit is the maximum unsigned short value. A message descriptor carries interrupt number and vectors used and device link and message and affinity and optional input output memory location and shift and optional system file attributes and message writer callback with private data and message index and either device specific or generic cookie data.
Descriptor filter distinguishes all descriptors and those without an associated interrupt and those with one. Per device domain storage pairs a dynamic index with the backing interrupt domain.

First descriptor lookup selects the default domain with a caller supplied filter. Domain iteration repeatedly advances through matching descriptors. Default domain iteration and device extraction and location recording and descriptor insertion and range freeing and full freeing all delegate to domain specific implementations with the default domain identifier.

Domain operations table provides hooks for hardware number translation and per interrupt initialization and release and device preparation and teardown and descriptor preparation and assignment and bulk allocation and release and firmware translation. Domain information records flags and bus token and size and operations and device and chip and data and flow handler with data and name and allocation data and private data. Template bundles a name buffer with chip and operations and information and allocation storage.
Message writer callback receives at least the descriptor being programmed with any further parameters not visible in the examined fragment.

Reverse iteration relies on a signed loop variable to terminate correctly including when the count is zero. Wrap tolerant predicates remain valid only within half the counter range. Tick conversions saturate at the maximum offset on overflow rather than wrapping.
